title: Multiplication and Division of Whole Numbers
seo_title: Multiplication and Division – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Multiply whole numbers by 2- and 3-digit numbers; divide by 1- and 2-digit numbers with and without remainders; solve word problems. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on long multiplication, short and long division, remainders and multiplication and division word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Division is the inverse of multiplication
body_html:
How to think about it

  • For 346 × 27, find 346 × 7 and 346 × 20, then add the two answers.
  • In division, share from the biggest place. Write any remainder at the end.
  • Check: 254 ÷ 7 = 36 remainder 2, because 36 × 7 + 2 = 254.

Examples

Example

346 × 27

346 × 7 = 2,422

346 × 20 = 6,920

Answer: 9,342

Example

918 ÷ 6

9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3, 31 ÷ 6 = 5 r 1, 18 ÷ 6 = 3

Answer: 153

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the 0 when multiplying by tens346 × 20: write a 0 first, then multiply by 2.
A remainder bigger than the divisorIf the remainder is not smaller than the divisor, the quotient is too small.
Dropping a zero in the quotientIn 612 ÷ 6 = 102, write the 0 in the tens place.

faq.q: How do I check a division?
faq.a: Multiply the quotient by the divisor and add the remainder.

items.q: Tobi works out 656 ÷ 4 = 111 r 2. What mistake did he make?
c: He divided by the wrong number
He did not carry the remainders
He missed a 0 in the answer
items.e: Tobi divided each digit on its own and threw the remainders away. Each remainder must be carried to the next digit. 6 ÷ 4 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 25; 25 ÷ 4 = 6 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Answer: 164. Check: 164 × 4 = 656.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 ÷ 7 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 7 = 3 r 3, carry the 3 to make 35; 35 ÷ 7 = 5. Answer: 135. Check: 135 × 7 = 945.

items.q: Use short division.

items.q: Use short division to work out 873 ÷ 9.
items.e: 9 does not go into 8, so carry the 8 to make 87; 87 ÷ 9 = 9 r 6, carry the 6 to make 63; 63 ÷ 9 = 7. Answer: 97. Check: 97 × 9 = 873.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 59; 59 ÷ 9 = 6 r 5, carry the 5 to make 54; 54 ÷ 9 = 6. Answer: 66. Check: 66 × 9 = 594.

items.q: Samuel uses short division for 753 ÷ 4. First, 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3. What does he divide next?
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3. The remainder 3 is 3 hundreds, which is 30 tens. Write it as a small 3 in front of the 5, so you divide 35 next: 35 ÷ 4 = 8 r 3. The whole answer: 188 r 1.

items.q: Babatunde uses short division for 972 ÷ 6. First, 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3. What does he divide next?
items.e: 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3. The remainder 3 is 3 hundreds, which is 30 tens. Write it as a small 3 in front of the 7, so you divide 37 next: 37 ÷ 6 = 6 r 1. The whole answer: 162.

items.q: Use short division to work out 888 ÷ 6.
items.e: 8 ÷ 6 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 6 = 4 r 4, carry the 4 to make 48; 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Answer: 148. Check: 148 × 6 = 888.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 4 ÷ 4 = 1; 4 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Answer: 106. Check: 106 × 4 = 424.

items.q: 378 ÷ 6 = 63. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 63 × 6 = 378, which matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: Use short division to work out 231 ÷ 6.
items.e: 6 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 6 = 3 r 5, carry the 5 to make 51; 51 ÷ 6 = 8 r 3. Answer: 38 r 3. Check: 38 × 6 + 3 = 231.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 6 ÷ 5 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 5 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 37; 37 ÷ 5 = 7 r 2. Answer: 127 r 2. Check: 127 × 5 + 2 = 637.

items.q: Use short division to work out 514 ÷ 4.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 4 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 4 = 8 r 2. Answer: 128 r 2. Check: 128 × 4 + 2 = 514.

items.q: What is the remainder when 656 is divided by 7?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the answer to the division. 7 does not go into 6, so carry the 6 to make 65; 65 ÷ 7 = 9 r 2, carry the 2 to make 26; 26 ÷ 7 = 3 r 5. Answer: 93 r 5. Check: 93 × 7 + 5 = 656.

items.q: Use short division to work out 747 ÷ 4.
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 4 = 8 r 2, carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 4 = 6 r 3. Answer: 186 r 3. Check: 186 × 4 + 3 = 747.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 ÷ 7 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 7 = 2 r 4, carry the 4 to make 43; 43 ÷ 7 = 6 r 1. Answer: 126 r 1. Check: 126 × 7 + 1 = 883.

items.q: You divide a number by 4. Which of these could be the remainder?
items.e: A remainder is always less than the divisor. When you divide by 4, the remainder can only be 1 to 3 (or 0). If you have 4 or more left, 4 goes in again.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 7 = 2 r 5, carry the 5 to make 51; 51 ÷ 7 = 7 r 2. Answer: 27 r 2. Check: 27 × 7 + 2 = 191.

items.q: What is the remainder when 584 is divided by 6?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the answer to the division. 6 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 58; 58 ÷ 6 = 9 r 4, carry the 4 to make 44; 44 ÷ 6 = 7 r 2. Answer: 97 r 2. Check: 97 × 6 + 2 = 584.

items.q: Use short division to work out 934 ÷ 5.
items.e: 9 ÷ 5 = 1 r 4, carry the 4 to make 43; 43 ÷ 5 = 8 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 5 = 6 r 4. Answer: 186 r 4. Check: 186 × 5 + 4 = 934.

items.e: Add the partial quotients: 30 + 10 + 1 = 41. Check: 41 × 26 = 1,066.

What is 3,465 ÷ 98?
items.e: 34 is less than 98, so start with 346. 346 ÷ 98 = 3: 3 × 98 = 294, 346 − 294 = 52. Bring down 5: 525 ÷ 98 = 5: 5 × 98 = 490, 525 − 490 = 35. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 35. Answer: 35 R 35. Check: 35 × 98 + 35 = 3,465.

items.q: What is 3,987 ÷ 94?
items.e: 39 is less than 94, so start with 398. 398 ÷ 94 = 4: 4 × 94 = 376, 398 − 376 = 22. Bring down 7: 227 ÷ 94 = 2: 2 × 94 = 188, 227 − 188 = 39. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 39. Answer: 42 R 39. Check: 42 × 94 + 39 = 3,987.

items.q: You divide 8,491 ÷ 39 with long division. Above which place do you write the first digit of the quotient?
items.e: 84 is at least 39, so start with 84 hundreds: 84 ÷ 39 = 2. The quotient is 217 R 28.

items.q: Use the area model to find 1,190 ÷ 35.
items.e: The model splits 1,190 into 1,050 + 140. Divide each part by 35: 1,050 ÷ 35 = 30, 140 ÷ 35 = 4. Add the partial quotients: 30 + 4 = 34. Check: 34 × 35 = 1,190.

items.q: Divide.

Divide.
items.e: 29 is less than 81, so start with 290. 290 ÷ 81 = 3: 3 × 81 = 243, 290 − 243 = 47. Bring down 8: 478 ÷ 81 = 5: 5 × 81 = 405, 478 − 405 = 73. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 73. Answer: 35 R 73. Check: 35 × 81 + 73 = 2,908.

items.q: How many digits does the quotient of 1,176 ÷ 73 have?
items.e: 11 is less than 73, so the quotient has no hundreds. Start with 117 tens. 1,176 ÷ 73 = 16 R 8, which has 2 digits.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 28 is less than 51, so start with 281. 281 ÷ 51 = 5: 5 × 51 = 255, 281 − 255 = 26. Bring down 5: 265 ÷ 51 = 5: 5 × 51 = 255, 265 − 255 = 10. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 10. Answer: 55 R 10. Check: 55 × 51 + 10 = 2,815.

items.q: A dripping tap wastes 45 ml of water every hour. How much water does it waste in 24 hours?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 hours × 45 ml, so multiply 45 × 24. Row 1: 45 × 4 = 180. Row 2: 45 × 20 = 900 (write the place-holder 0, then 45 × 2 = 90). Add: 180 + 900 = 1,080.

items.q: A rabbit has a mass of 2,400 g. A guinea pig is 14 as heavy. What is the mass of the guinea pig?
items.e: “14 as heavy” means divide into 4 equal parts: 2,400 ÷ 4 = 600 g. Multiplying by 4 gives 9,600 g, which is heavier, not lighter.

items.q: A bakery bakes 2,350 bread rolls every day. How many rolls does it bake in 6 days?
items.e: Equal groups: 6 days × 2,350 rolls, so multiply 2,350 × 6. Units: 0 × 6 = 0. Write 0. Tens: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3. Hundreds: 3 × 6 + 3 = 21. Write 1, exchange 2. Thousands: 2 × 6 + 2 = 14. Write 14. Answer: 14,100.

items.q: Hadiza cycles 18 km every day for 14 days. How far does she cycle altogether?
items.e: Equal groups: 14 days × 18 km, so multiply 18 × 14. Row 1: 18 × 4 = 72. Row 2: 18 × 10 = 180 (write the place-holder 0, then 18 × 1 = 18). Add: 72 + 180 = 252.

items.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 175 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 12 people?
items.e: 12 people is 3 times as many as 4 people (4 × 3 = 12), so use 3 times as much flour: 175 × 3 = 525 g. Do not multiply by 12: the recipe is for 4 people, not 1.

items.q: A box holds 144 pencils. The school office orders 23 boxes. How many pencils is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 23 boxes × 144 pencils, so multiply 144 × 23. Row 1: 144 × 3 = 432. Row 2: 144 × 20 = 2,880 (write the place-holder 0, then 144 × 2 = 288). Add: 432 + 2,880 = 3,312.

items.q: A lorry carries 32 crates. Each crate has a mass of 145 kg. What is the total mass of the crates?
items.e: Equal groups: 32 crates × 145 kg, so multiply 145 × 32. Row 1: 145 × 2 = 290. Row 2: 145 × 30 = 4,350 (write the place-holder 0, then 145 × 3 = 435). Add: 290 + 4,350 = 4,640.

items.q: A crate holds 24 bottles of milk. The school orders 35 crates this term. How many bottles is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 35 crates × 24 bottles, so multiply 24 × 35. Row 1: 24 × 5 = 120. Row 2: 24 × 30 = 720 (write the place-holder 0, then 24 × 3 = 72). Add: 120 + 720 = 840.

items.q: A family uses 165 litres of water a day. How much water do they use in a week?
items.e: Equal groups: 7 days × 165 litres, so multiply 165 × 7. Units: 5 × 7 = 35. Write 5, exchange 3. Tens: 6 × 7 + 3 = 45. Write 5, exchange 4. Hundreds: 1 × 7 + 4 = 11. Write 11. Answer: 1,155.

items.q: A printer prints 36 pages a minute. How many pages does it print in 25 minutes?
items.e: Equal groups: 25 minutes × 36 pages, so multiply 36 × 25. Row 1: 36 × 5 = 180. Row 2: 36 × 20 = 720 (write the place-holder 0, then 36 × 2 = 72). Add: 180 + 720 = 900.

items.q: Tolu runs 2,136 m by running 8 laps of the school field. Each lap is the same length. How long is one lap?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 8 = 2 r 5, carry the 5 to make 53; 53 ÷ 8 = 6 r 5, carry the 5 to make 56; 56 ÷ 8 = 7. So 2,136 ÷ 8 = 267. There is no remainder, so the answer is 267 m.

items.q: There are 132 children at a netball tournament. Each team needs exactly 7 players. How many full teams can be made?
items.e: Divide: 7 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 7 = 1 r 6, carry the 6 to make 62; 62 ÷ 7 = 8 r 6. So 132 ÷ 7 = 18 r 6. The 6 children left over are not enough to make another team, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 18 teams.

items.q: 29 pizzas are shared equally between 8 tables at a party. How much pizza does each table get?
items.e: Divide: 29 ÷ 8 = 3 r 5. The 5 left over can be shared too: 5 ÷ 8 = 58. Each gets 3 58 pizzas.

items.q: Uju is putting 419 photos into an album. Each page holds 6 photos. How many pages does she need?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 4, so carry the 4 to make 41; 41 ÷ 6 = 6 r 5, carry the 5 to make 59; 59 ÷ 6 = 9 r 5. So 419 ÷ 6 = 69 r 5. 69 pages are not enough: 5 photos would still need a page. You need 1 more, so the answer is 70 pages.

items.q: 339 playing cards are dealt out equally to 6 players. Each player gets as many as possible. How many cards are left over?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 6 = 5 r 3, carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 6 = 6 r 3. So 339 ÷ 6 = 56 r 3. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 3 cards.

items.q: Babatunde swims 2,625 m in 5 days. He swims the same distance every day. How far does he swim each day?
items.e: Divide: 5 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 26; 26 ÷ 5 = 5 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 5 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 25; 25 ÷ 5 = 5. So 2,625 ÷ 5 = 525. There is no remainder, so the answer is 525 m.

items.q: A farm collects 1,822 eggs. It packs them in boxes of 6. How many boxes does it need for all the eggs?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 6 = 3; 6 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 2 to make 22; 22 ÷ 6 = 3 r 4. So 1,822 ÷ 6 = 303 r 4. 303 boxes are not enough: 4 eggs would still need a box. You need 1 more, so the answer is 304 boxes.

items.q: 169 people are coming to a school concert. The chairs are put out in rows of 9. How many rows are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 9 = 1 r 7, carry the 7 to make 79; 79 ÷ 9 = 8 r 7. So 169 ÷ 9 = 18 r 7. 18 rows are not enough: 7 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so the answer is 19 rows.

items.q: 199 pupils are going to a museum. Each minibus has 8 seats for pupils. How many minibuses are needed?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 8 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 8 = 4 r 7. So 199 ÷ 8 = 24 r 7. 24 minibuses are not enough: 7 pupils would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so the answer is 25 minibuses.

items.q: A farm has 1,534 eggs. It packs them in boxes of 6. How many boxes can it fill completely?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 6 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 6 = 5 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 6 = 5 r 4. So 1,534 ÷ 6 = 255 r 4. The 4 eggs left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 255 boxes.
